learningObjectives: Define the responsibilities of key roles in Pega project delivery
Match each role to the studio(s) they use
Explain how Workspaces and Branches enable isolated parallel development
Monitor Branch health with Branch quality metrics

elements.term: Delivery roles: PO, Project Manager, Scrum Master
items: PRODUCT OWNER — manages scope and prioritizes sprint requirements
PROJECT MANAGER — leads delivery, maintains governance, liaises with client leadership
SCRUM MASTER — runs Sprint ceremonies (Planning, Sizing, Backlog Refinement, Retrospectives) and removes impediments

elements.text: Think of specialists preparing separate proposals, reviewing their work together, and integrating approved changes. Isolation reduces interference; it does not remove the need to resolve conflicting edits.

elements.term: Build & quality roles: SA/SSA/LSA, QA, BA
elements.description: Three build and quality assurance roles:
items: SYSTEM ARCHITECTS (SA/SSA/LSA) — configure the application; LSA imports Blueprint files
QUALITY ANALYSTS — verify requirements and write test scripts
BUSINESS ARCHITECT — translates business needs into workflows, Data Models, and user experiences

elements.term: Client & design roles: SME, UX, Solutions Consultant
items: SUBJECT MATTER EXPERT — client operational expert who supplies requirements
UX DESIGNER — ensures design meets user needs and accessibility standards
SOLUTIONS CONSULTANT — engages client in sales, co-designs Blueprint, hands off to delivery team

elements.description: Each studio serves a different set of roles:
items: APP STUDIO (no-code) — SAs, BAs, UX designers, solutions consultants, Project Managers, Scrum Masters
DEV STUDIO (advanced) — System Architects and Quality Analysts
PREDICTION STUDIO — data scientists
ADMIN STUDIO — business IT for system administration

elements.description: Three parallel development scopes (changes promote outward):
items: WORKSPACE — one developer's PRIVATE changes, isolated until shared
BRANCH — the TEAM's active changes in progress
APPLICATION — shared application configuration after integration; merging does not itself deploy a production release.

elements.description: Private development space tied to one operator and one application. Changes stay isolated until shared to a Branch — avoiding rule conflicts. Each operator gets one Workspace by default; multiple are allowed. Enabled via the EnableWorkspace setting.

A BRANCH is a container of Rulesets under active development. Branch Rulesets are based on (branched from) another Ruleset. Best practice: one Branch per feature so teams work in isolation — a finished feature merges independently.

A Branch merges into the main application only after the feature is complete, conflicts are resolved, and approval is granted. Pega automatically checks which Rules are new or updated before completing the merge.

Production release is a separate step.</desc><rect x="10" y="15" width="740" height="150" rx="12" fill="var(--pa-surface-1)" stroke="var(--pa-brand)"/><g fill="var(--pa-ink)" font-family="system-ui" font-size="17"><text x="32" y="50">Workspace → Feature branch → Shared application rules</text><text x="32" y="88">Review changes, tests and potential conflicts before merging.</text><text x="32" y="126">Merge is integration; production release is a separate operation.</text></g></svg>
elements.caption: The Workspace example flows through a feature Branch to shared application rules. This is not a universal locked-base prerequisite or a deployment guarantee.

elements.description: Settings that flag elements not complying with Pega best practices. You must respond to warnings to keep the application efficient. The WEIGHTED SCORE metric reflects the number and severity of guardrail warnings on a Branch.
Four metrics tracked per Branch before merging:
items: (1) GUARDRAILS — weighted compliance score
(2) MERGE CONFLICTS — potential conflicts to investigate
(3) TEST COVERAGE & UNIT TESTS — rules covered % and pass rate %
(4) UNCOVERED RULES — Branch Rules not covered by any test

elements.title: Studio & Role Assignment Decisions

examPitfalls.title: Role responsibilities
examPitfalls.trapDescription: PO = scope + sprint priorities; Project Manager = governance/liaison; Scrum Master = ceremonies + removes impediments; LSA imports Blueprint; Solutions Consultant co-designs the Blueprint early in sales.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Match each responsibility to the right role — these are common scenario questions.

examPitfalls.title: Roles ↔ studios
examPitfalls.trapDescription: App Studio serves most roles (PM docs, Scrum user stories); Dev Studio serves SAs + QAs; Prediction Studio = data scientists; Admin Studio = IT.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Map each team role to its primary Studio: SA/LSA use Dev Studio for technical work; Citizen Developers and BAs use App Studio for configuration.

examPitfalls.title: Workspace = one operator, one application
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A Workspace is private to one operator and one app (one by default, can create multiple); changes stay private until shared to a Branch.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Enable and use Workspaces for private development where supported. Sharing changes still requires review for possible conflicts.

examPitfalls.title: Branch Rulesets
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask where new rules created during parallel development are stored. Candidates say 'the main application Ruleset.' Rules created during team development are stored in Branch Rulesets — they are merged back into the main Ruleset when the branch is complete.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Create a Branch Ruleset per feature or developer to isolate work — merge back into the main Ruleset only after the feature is complete, conflict-free, and approved.

examPitfalls.title: Merge prerequisites
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A Branch merges into the main application only after the feature is complete, conflicts are resolved, and approval is granted.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Don't merge until complete + conflict-free + approved; the system auto-checks updated/new Rules.

examPitfalls.title: Branch quality metrics
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The four metrics are Guardrails (Weighted score), Merge conflicts (Total), Test coverage/Unit tests (Rules covered %, Test pass rate %), and Uncovered Rules.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review guardrail warnings, potential merge conflicts, test coverage and pass results, and uncovered Rules. Approval is a separate review decision, not the fourth metric.

examPitfalls.title: Isolation still needs integration review
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Separate development does not prove that changed Rules will merge without conflicts or that a merged feature has been deployed.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review the feature and resolve conflicts before approved integration; verify a release separately.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Who manages the project scope and prioritizes requirements in sprints so each release delivers business value?

options.text: The Product Owner (PO)
The Scrum Master
The Lead System Architect
The UX Designer

practiceQuiz.hint: Managing scope and prioritizing sprint requirements defines the Product Owner role.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Scope and sprint priorities identify the Product Owner responsibility.

optionExplanations.A: Scope and sprint priorities identify the Product Owner responsibility.
optionExplanations.B: Ceremony facilitation does not identify the prioritization duty asked for.
optionExplanations.C: Technical architecture is distinct from the stated business prioritization.
optionExplanations.D: Usability work is distinct from owning these scope priorities.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which role facilitates Sprint Planning, Sizing, Backlog Refinement, and Retrospectives and removes impediments?

options.text: The Scrum Master
The Project Manager
The Product Owner
The Subject Matter Expert

practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the Scrum role responsible for facilitating ceremonies and removing team impediments.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Scrum facilitation and impediment removal identify this responsibility.

optionExplanations.A: Scrum facilitation and impediment removal identify this responsibility.
optionExplanations.B: Delivery governance is different from facilitating the named Scrum activities.
optionExplanations.C: Backlog priorities are different from this facilitation duty.
optionExplanations.D: Operational expertise does not identify the requested Scrum responsibility.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Who is responsible for importing Blueprint files into Pega Platform and configuring functional and technical requirements from user stories?

options.text: The Lead System Architect (LSA)
The Business Architect
The Quality Analyst
The Solutions Consultant

practiceQuiz.hint: Which team role is responsible for importing Blueprint files into Pega Platform?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The role description assigns this Blueprint import responsibility to the LSA.

optionExplanations.A: The role description assigns this Blueprint import responsibility to the LSA.
optionExplanations.B: Business analysis does not identify the import responsibility in this role mapping.
optionExplanations.C: Test design does not identify the required Blueprint import responsibility.
optionExplanations.D: Co-design and handoff are distinct from the described platform import.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which role engages the client early in the sales process and co-designs the Blueprint before handing it to the delivery team?

options.text: The Solutions Consultant
The Project Manager
The Scrum Master
The Quality Analyst

practiceQuiz.hint: Which role engages the client during pre-sales and co-designs the Blueprint before delivery?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Solutions Consultant is associated with the early sales and Blueprint handoff requirement. The other named duties do not identify that responsibility; project staffing is not universally restricted to separate phases.

optionExplanations.A: Early engagement and Blueprint handoff identify this role.
optionExplanations.B: Project governance does not identify this pre-sales requirement.
optionExplanations.C: Scrum facilitation does not identify this Blueprint sales responsibility.
optionExplanations.D: Verification duties do not identify the described co-design handoff.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A new Pega project team is being onboarded and the project lead needs to determine which team members require access to Dev Studio for their day-to-day development and configuration work. Which TWO roles in a Pega project primarily use Dev Studio?

options.text: System Architects
Quality Analysts
Data scientists
Business-related IT administrators

practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the two roles whose primary workspace is Dev Studio for technical build and test work.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Technical architects use advanced configuration tools for this work. Quality analysts use the technical authoring space for verification work.

optionExplanations.A: Technical architects use advanced configuration tools for this work.
optionExplanations.B: Quality analysts use the technical authoring space for verification work.
optionExplanations.C: Prediction tooling serves the stated analytics role.
optionExplanations.D: Administration tooling serves the stated operations role.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is explaining Pega's parallel development approach to a team that must build three independent features simultaneously without their changes colliding. A developer asks how their personal development environment is isolated from teammates. What is a Workspace in Pega parallel development?

options.text: A secure space tied to ONE operator and ONE application; changes stay private until shared to a Branch
A shared team area where all developers' changes are immediately visible to everyone
A versioned container of released application features
A Work Queue for development tasks

practiceQuiz.hint: A Workspace is private, tied to one operator and exactly one application.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The private development scope belongs to the specified operator and application.

optionExplanations.A: The private development scope belongs to the specified operator and application.
optionExplanations.B: Immediate team visibility contradicts the private scope in this example.
optionExplanations.C: Released application configuration is not the private workspace.
optionExplanations.D: Assignment routing is different from isolating development changes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How many Workspaces can an operator have within an application, and how are Workspaces turned on?

options.text: One by default, but the operator can create multiple; Workspaces are enabled with the EnableWorkspace setting
Exactly one, always; they are on by default and cannot be disabled
Unlimited and shared across applications; no setting is required
One per Work Group; enabled in Admin Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: Default is one Workspace per operator; multiple allowed; EnableWorkspace setting required.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The topic specifies a default workspace and permits more, with feature enablement.

optionExplanations.A: The topic specifies a default workspace and permits more, with feature enablement.
optionExplanations.B: The documented model permits multiple workspaces and enablement.
optionExplanations.C: The workspace association does not span unrelated applications as claimed.
optionExplanations.D: A group routing relationship does not own the developer workspace.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega project team is about to develop three features in parallel. The SA recommends that each feature be developed in its own Branch Ruleset. A junior developer who is unfamiliar with the concept asks for a definition. What is a Branch Ruleset in Pega Platform?

options.text: A Ruleset that is based on (branched from) another Ruleset and holds the Rules in active development in that Branch
A standalone Ruleset with no relationship to any other Ruleset
A Ruleset that stores only released, generally available Rules
A copy of the entire application database

practiceQuiz.hint: Branch Rulesets are based on another Ruleset and hold currently in-development Rules.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A branch ruleset derives from another ruleset for active feature changes.

optionExplanations.A: A branch ruleset derives from another ruleset for active feature changes.
optionExplanations.B: The definition expressly includes the relationship to a base ruleset.
optionExplanations.C: Active development differs from exclusively released rules.
optionExplanations.D: A development rule container is not a complete database copy.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A junior SA asks a senior team lead when a development Branch in Pega can be merged back into the main application Ruleset. Under what conditions does a Branch qualify to merge into the main application?

options.text: Only after the feature is complete, conflicts are resolved, and approval is granted
Immediately and automatically as soon as any Rule is changed in the Branch
Only when all other Branches are also complete
Never — Branches cannot be merged, only deleted

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall the three conditions that must all be true before a Branch can be merged into the main application.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The described review process requires completed, reviewed integration.

optionExplanations.A: The described review process requires completed, reviewed integration.
optionExplanations.B: Editing one rule does not itself initiate the described approved merge.
optionExplanations.C: Separate features can complete and integrate at different times.
optionExplanations.D: Merging is supported; deleting is not the only operation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team wants to check, before merging, how many of their Branch Rules are covered by tests. Which Branch quality metric shows this?

options.text: Test coverage / Unit tests — e.g., the Rules covered and Test pass rate metrics
The Weighted score guardrail metric
Total merge conflicts
Uncovered Rules only — there is no coverage percentage

practiceQuiz.rationale: Coverage percentage and test results provide the requested testing evidence.

optionExplanations.A: Coverage percentage and test results provide the requested testing evidence.
optionExplanations.B: Guardrail warnings do not measure how many rules tests cover.
optionExplanations.C: Conflict counts do not measure testing coverage.
optionExplanations.D: The metric set includes coverage percentage as well as uncovered rules.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team lead is reviewing a development Branch before approving it for merge. Which TWO are Branch quality metrics that Pega uses to judge whether a Branch is ready to merge?

options.text: Guardrails (Weighted score) — number and severity of best-practice warnings
Merge conflicts (Total merge conflicts) — potential conflicts to resolve
Operator Urgency — the priority of the developer's worklist
Ruleset lock count — how many Rulesets are locked

practiceQuiz.hint: Which two Branch quality metrics are used to assess whether a Branch is ready to merge?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The weighted warning score is a documented quality signal. Potential merge conflicts are another documented quality signal.

optionExplanations.A: The weighted warning score is a documented quality signal.
optionExplanations.B: Potential merge conflicts are another documented quality signal.
optionExplanations.C: Work routing urgency is not this branch quality measure.
optionExplanations.D: A lock count is not one of the quality metrics listed here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the documented Locations example, changes start privately, are shared with the feature team, and are then merged before a release. What is that example’s sequence?

options.text: Workspace → Feature Branch → Application integration, before release
Application → Branch → Workspace
Branch → Workspace → Application
Workspace → Application directly, skipping the Branch

practiceQuiz.hint: This is the example’s integration sequence, not a claim that merging publishes production.
practiceQuiz.rationale: This follows the example’s private, team and shared integration stages.

optionExplanations.A: This follows the example’s private, team and shared integration stages.
optionExplanations.B: This reverses the example’s progression from private development.
optionExplanations.C: This puts private work after team sharing in the example.
optionExplanations.D: This omits the example’s team feature review stage.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega project includes System Architects, Business Architects, and developers working in parallel. Which TWO statements correctly describe how roles align with the Pega development environment?

options.text: System Architects primarily use Dev Studio to configure low-level technical Rules and advanced configurations
Business Architects use App Studio for supported business configuration; advanced Rule types can require other access
All team members must use Dev Studio for any Rule configuration — App Studio is view-only and cannot edit Rules
Business Architects and System Architects use identical studios with the same feature sets and no difference in access

practiceQuiz.hint: SA = Dev Studio for technical depth; BA = App Studio for business configuration without code.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Advanced technical configuration fits the technical studio described. Supported business configuration fits App Studio; access still depends on tasks.

optionExplanations.A: Advanced technical configuration fits the technical studio described.
optionExplanations.B: Supported business configuration fits App Studio; access still depends on tasks.
optionExplanations.C: App Studio provides editing capability, not just viewing.
optionExplanations.D: The studios expose different tools; roles do not imply identical access.

quickRecap.value: PO (scope + sprint priorities) · Project Manager (governance/liaison/schedule-budget-scope) · Scrum Master (ceremonies + removes impediments).
SA/SSA/LSA (LSA imports Blueprint) · QA (scenario tests) · BA (workflows/Data Model/UX).
SME (operational knowledge, walkthroughs) · UX (accessibility/consistency) · Solutions Consultant (co-designs Blueprint early in sales).
App (most + PM docs + Scrum user stories) · Dev (SAs/QAs) · Prediction (data scientists) · Admin (IT).
Private; 1 operator + 1 app (default one, can create many); App+Dev Studio; EnableWorkspace; private until shared to a Branch.
